newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand hits new low.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand hits new low.

text.p: The South African rand received a fresh mauling on the foreign exchange markets on Tuesday, hitting a new all-time low of 4.69 against the dollar.

Dealers said the South Africa's central Reserve Bank stepped in to support the currency, offering dollars into a tense market. That pulled the rand back from its weakest levels but the unit remained weak and dealers predicted it could test the 4.70 level later in the day.
"With all the gloomy headlines in the newpapers, people are going to be a little bit scared today," said one rand trader.
The currency woes took their toll on other South African markets with long bond yields kicking up to the highest level since June at just under 16 percent.
Shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange shed more than one percent of their value by mid-morning as investors baled out fearing further rand losses.

Dealers said the market was still concerned at the worsening inflation picture, high credit growth and downbeat remarks by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals who warned monetary policy might need to be tightened further if there was no decline in credit growth.

Much of the pressure on the rand continued to come from overseas investors, fearful about the country's economic problems, including balance of payments difficulties and low foreign reserves, dealers said.

The rand has now lost more than 28 percent of its value against the dollar since mid-February when the run on the currency first started on ill-founded rumours about President Nelson Mandela's health and talk of an imminent scrapping of exchange controls.
